summary: TelegramCommandParser + ParsedCommand are a clean, AC-compliant pure utility. All edge cases from the task matrix (null, empty, slash-only, leading whitespace, @botname strip on first @, multi-space trim, newline/tab splitters, case preservation, /start@ empty bot, /start@@x multiple @) are handled correctly and pinned by tests. Round-1 javadoc-drift fix on ParsedCommand and the test-consistency fix were both applied correctly in 7dea05d.

suggestions.suggestion: Consider sealing the utility further by adding @SuppressWarnings("unused") on the private constructor or marking the class with a package-private javadoc tag, but this is purely cosmetic — the throwing private ctor + final class already block instantiation and subclassing.
suggestions.benefit: Slightly clearer intent for static analysers; not behavioural.

suggestions.suggestion: The leading-whitespace-skip loop uses Character.isWhitespace(char) on a single char; the splitter loop on line 45 uses the (int) overload via auto-promotion. Both work identically for BMP code points but the difference may confuse future readers. Use the same overload in both places.
suggestions.benefit: Stylistic consistency; no behavioural change (Telegram payloads are UTF-16 strings and surrogate-pair whitespace is not a realistic input).

suggestions.suggestion: The NOT_A_COMMAND sentinel is cached as a private static final — nice. Could optionally expose it as a public static final EMPTY constant for callers that want identity comparison instead of .equals(), but the notACommand() factory is sufficient and intent-revealing as-is.
suggestions.benefit: Marginal micro-optimisation if call sites want == rather than .equals(); zero allocation cost either way since the factory already returns the cached instance.
